step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify nodes from visual evidence and transcript:
   - External input: 'Expedia Group' (ThirdParty).
   - Batch processing layer: 'S3' (data lake bucket), 'EC2' (custom Parquet/bookmark transformation host), 'Glue' (ETL service), and 'S3 (CSV)' (destination bucket formatted for Salesforce).
   - Real-time processing layer: 'ECS' (running Kafka consumer), 'Aurora' (MySQL engine for aggregation/sorting), 'Lambda' (processing logic), 'SQS' (queueing messages), and destination 'Salesforce' (Einstein Analytics reporting engine).
2. Construct logical flows:
   - Flow 0 (Batch pipeline): Expedia Group -> S3 ingestion bucket -> EC2 / Glue (parallel branches) -> S3 (CSV) output bucket.
   - Flow 1 (Real-time stream): ECS -> Aurora -> Lambda -> SQS -> Salesforce.
3. Validate attributes against schemas and allowed vocabulary list.

graph.name: Expedia Group Integration with Salesforce Einstein Analytics
graph.categories: Batch Processing, Real-Time Streaming, Data Lake & Analytics
graph.notes: Architecture processes 500 to 800 million rows per day via batch processing (top layer) and 5 to 10 million events per day via real-time streaming (bottom layer) to populate Salesforce Einstein Analytics.

nodes.name: Expedia Group
nodes.notes: Source applications (on-prem and cloud) providing booking and partner data in diverse formats (Parquet, CSV, JSON).

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Data ingestion layer / data lake bucket receiving daily batch data from Expedia Group applications.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Handles custom processing and transformations (e.g., Parquet file bookmarking) where Glue had limitations.

nodes.name: Glue
nodes.notes: Serverless ETL service used to transform heterogeneous source data into a unified structure.

nodes.name: S3 (CSV)
nodes.notes: Output bucket storing transformed CSV files suitable for Salesforce Einstein Analytics.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Runs Kafka consumer tasks processing 5 to 10 million real-time events per day.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: MySQL-compatible database engine used for aggregating and sorting real-time streaming data.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes data processing functions and prepares queueable messages.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Message queue holding event payloads before final ingestion into Salesforce.

nodes.name: Salesforce
nodes.notes: Salesforce Einstein Analytics reporting engine destination providing business insights.

edges.notes: Expedia applications ingest heterogeneous batch data daily into S3 bucket.
S3 data routed to EC2 for Parquet and custom transformations.
S3 data routed to AWS Glue for standard ETL transformations.
EC2 outputs converted CSV data into destination S3 bucket.
Glue writes transformed CSV data into destination S3 bucket.
ECS Kafka consumer processes streaming events and writes to Aurora.
Aggregated data from Aurora is processed by Lambda.
Lambda queues formatted messages into SQS.
Messages from SQS are pushed into Salesforce Einstein Analytics.
